brief_figures.prepaid_rto_note: BRIEF-GIVEN, NOT verified from the data file: orders_sample.csv contains only COD orders (2,018 of 2,018), so no prepaid RTO rate can be computed from it.

costs.note: per_rto_cost = 65 + 65 + 25 + (0.08 x 180) = 169.40, from the assignment brief

first_time_buyer_protection.fake_name_exception: Fake/test names (test, asdf, qwerty, abc, xyz and similar patterns) are treated as not-a-real-order, so the cap does not apply to them.
first_time_buyer_protection.rule: A first-time buyer (customer_prior_orders = 0) is NEVER auto-cancelled, unless the name looks fake or test-like. First-timers are capped at 'Nudge to prepaid'. Cancelling a genuine first order wastes the Rs 300+ spent acquiring that customer and they rarely come back.

high_risk_states_note: States with an Apr-Aug 2026 training RTO rate of 38% or higher on at least 50 orders (Bihar 52.3%, Uttar Pradesh 48.1%, Madhya Pradesh 38.3%). Pincode-level lists are deliberately NOT used: the file has 1,067 distinct pincodes for 2,017 resolved orders and no pincode has more than 12 orders, so pincode history is noise, not signal.

llm_line.code_does_better: Everything numeric and checkable: prior RTO counts, address length and digit checks, state rates, thresholds, discount maths, and the decision itself. These must be exact, repeatable and auditable, so they stay in deterministic code.
llm_line.llm_helps: Judging whether an address is complete and real, spotting novel fake names, and reading Hinglish addresses — all language-judgement tasks where wording varies too much for fixed rules.
llm_line.runtime_status: This submission ships with a deterministic checker that covers every fake-name and address pattern actually observed in the data file, plus a documented LLM hook (llm_address_check in cod_engine.py) for the judgement cases. No live LLM key is wired in and no live LLM call is claimed: the deterministic path is what runs, and the hook shows exactly where a model would plug in and what it would be asked.

prepaid_discount.note: 5% off, capped at Rs 40. Maths: expected RTO cost per COD order is 28.4% x Rs 169.40 = Rs 48.11; per prepaid order it is 4% x Rs 169.40 = Rs 6.78 (prepaid rate is brief-given). Saving per converted order is about Rs 41.33, so the discount must stay under Rs 41.33. An uncapped 5% would cost Rs 150 on a Rs 2,999 order and lose money, hence the cap. The discount is only paid when the customer actually converts, so the per-converted-order comparison is the right one.

score_weights.address_rule_note: Short-address and no-digit points do NOT stack: every short address in the data already lacks a digit, so the engine takes the larger of the two, never both.

thresholds.note: Score >= 70 -> Hold/cancel; 45-69 -> Nudge to prepaid; 25-44 -> Ship after confirmation; below 25 -> Ship as-is. Edit these numbers in this file to change behaviour without touching code.

whatsapp.language_note: Messages go out in Hinglish (Roman script) with a short English line. The order data shows customers themselves write addresses in Hinglish ('Station chowk se left, Hanuman Mandir ke saamne'), so confirmation in the customer's own register is the one most likely to be answered. Hinglish addresses returned at 30.8% RTO, close to the 28.4% average, so Hinglish is normal here — it is never scored as a risk signal.
